newsitem.title: USA: Pharmacyclics needs more tests on Gadolite.
newsitem.headline: Pharmacyclics needs more tests on Gadolite.

text.p: Pharmacyclics Inc on Wednesday said it will have to conduct more tests on its product, Gadolite, which will delay any filings for U.S. Food and Drug Administration approval by at least 18 months.
"We are disappointed that there will be a significant delay in the anticipated launch of Gadolite in the United States," Richard Miller, chief executive officer, said in a statement.
Gadolite is a medical diagnostic product that is being developed as a contrast agent used in magnetic resonance imaging to enhance delineation of the bowel.
In a statement, Pharmacyclics said it decided to conduct the additional tests after meeting with FDA officials in response to requests for additional information by the regulatory agency.
"The clinical efficacy and safety of Gadolite were not at issue during these discussions," Miller said. "
Pharmacyclics said the additional tests will test the stability of Gadolite.
The company noted Gadolite is of a lesser priority to the company than are its therapeutic products, Gd-Tex and Lu-Tex. Those products are curently in human trials.
